holidays.name: Star Wars Day
holidays.description: Fans around the world greet each other with 'May the Fourth be with you!' and celebrate with movie marathons, themed costumes, and lightsaber duels in the living room.
holidays.origin: The pun on 'May the Force be with you' dates back at least to 1979, when the Conservative Party placed a congratulatory ad in the London Evening News after Margaret Thatcher became Prime Minister. The date then grew into a fan holiday, and Disney and Lucasfilm made it an official marketing event after acquiring Star Wars.
holidays.funFact: The 1979 Thatcher ad read 'May the Fourth Be With You, Maggie. Congratulations.' Star Wars fans only picked up the pun decades later.

holidays.name: International Respect for Chickens Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate chickens as intelligent, social, and surprisingly complex birds rather than just a menu item. Backyard keepers and animal lovers honor their feathered friends.
holidays.origin: The observance was created by animal welfare advocates to promote compassion toward chickens and raise awareness of how they are treated in farming.
holidays.funFact: Chickens can recognize more than 100 different faces of people or other chickens and have been shown to display self-control while waiting for a larger food reward.

holidays.name: Orange Juice Day
holidays.description: A sunny celebration of the breakfast staple, encouraging everyone to raise a glass of OJ and toast the citrus that wakes up the world each morning.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that grew from the popularity of orange juice as a breakfast drink and citrus industry promotion, especially in orange-growing regions like Florida and California.
holidays.funFact: Frozen concentrated orange juice was developed in the 1940s, partly to give American soldiers a source of vitamin C, and it was among the first major frozen food successes.

holidays.name: National Renewal Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to refreshing your mind, home, and habits. People use it to declutter, start a new routine, or simply reset after a long stretch of busyness.
holidays.origin: This is a grassroots, unofficial observance promoted by wellness and self-improvement communities as a mid-spring chance for a fresh start.
holidays.funFact: Many people celebrate with spring cleaning projects. Studies suggest that decluttering a space can noticeably reduce feelings of stress.

holidays.name: International Firefighters' Day
holidays.description: A day honoring firefighters worldwide, with ceremonies, thank-you notes, and blue and red ribbons worn in tribute to those who risk their lives to protect others.
holidays.origin: It was established after five firefighters died in a bushfire in Linton, Victoria, Australia, in January 1999. An email called for a day of remembrance and recognition, and May 4 was chosen because it is the feast day of St. Florian, the patron saint of firefighters.
holidays.funFact: St. Florian was a Roman soldier who reportedly organized firefighting brigades, and he is often depicted pouring water from a bucket onto a burning house.
